method: Scoped validation for a brand-new skill (skill-usage-audit) plus a NOT-clause added to skill-routing-maintenance's description. Per skill-routing-maintenance's own scoping guidance, ran only the new entries plus the near-neighbors most likely to now compete (skill-routing-maintenance, skill-creator). One Haiku judge per query (model: claude-haiku-4-5), each shown ONLY a name+description listing for the meta-skill family plus generic fallbacks and the query text — no shared context between judges.

runs.query: We just spent this whole session adding a new CFGVer example -- can you check whether we used the right skills throughout, and whether anything we looked up by hand along the way should really have been documented in a skill instead?
Were all the skills triggered when needed? Did you have to look up any information that should have been available upon triggering a skill?
runs.note: anchors the skill's own core trigger phrase (the literal query that prompted its creation)

runs.query: The cfgver-memory skill isn't firing for a query about the _with_mem variants, can you check why and fix its trigger?
runs.note: regression check (was Q51): a single, already-identified misfire still stays skill-routing-maintenance's territory with skill-usage-audit now in the family

runs.query: I want to build a brand new skill for auto-generating changelogs from our commit messages -- nothing like it exists yet, help me draft it from scratch.
runs.note: regression check (was Q50): drafting a genuinely new skill from scratch still stays skill-creator's territory

summary: 4/4 pass, 0 regressions. skill-usage-audit fires correctly on both its target should-trigger cases (Q61, Q64) without stealing skill-routing-maintenance's or skill-creator's existing territory (Q62, Q63 both unchanged from their prior verdicts).
